newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Leumi sale price 10 pct over minimum.
newsitem.headline: Leumi sale price 10 pct over minimum.

text.p: A public offering in Bank Leumi, Israel's second largest bank, closed more than 10 percent above the minimum price, one of the underwriters said on Wednesday.
The I.B.I. investment house said the closing price was 11.2 shekels for a package of shares and warrants.
The offering for 15 percent of Leumi's share capital was 2.8 times oversubscribed, I.B.I. said.

The government will receive more than one billion shekels from the sale -- about 600 million shekels in cash and the rest with the exercise of warrants, some by the end of the year and the remainder in August 1998.
If all the warrants are exercised, the government will hold 66 percent of Leumi.

Finance Minister Dan Meridor said in a statement on Tuesday night that the sale would enable the government to raise three billion shekels from bank privatisations this year, not counting the proceeds from a tender offer now underway for a controlling stake in Bank Hapoalim.
"It should be noted that the completion of the Bank Hapoalim controlling stake could increase the government's proceeds in 1997-1998 by an additional three billion shekels," the Treasury said.
The tender is for 25 to 70 percent of Hapoalim, Israel's largest bank, and is due to be completed by the end of August.
The Leumi offering marks the second big public offering in the government's bank privatisation programme this year. In April, it sold 19 percent of Israel Discount Bank for 620 million shekels.
On Tuesday, the Treasury announced that the Ofer-Wertheim group would exercise an option to take another 25 percent of United Mizrahi Bank for approximately 450 million shekels.
Ofer-Wertheim has a controlling minority stake in Mizrahi, and the Treasury said the sale would reduce the government's stake in Mizrahi to 46 percent.
